preconditions.description: The number of towns n, roads m, goods types k, and required types s satisfy the given bounds.

preconditions.expression: len(a) == n and all(1 <= x <= k for x in a) and set(a) == set(range(1, k + 1))
preconditions.description: The goods array a has length n, contains values between 1 and k, and every type from 1 to k appears at least once.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n and u != v for u, v in roads)
preconditions.description: Each road connects two distinct towns within the valid range.
The number of road descriptions matches m.
The graph formed by towns and roads is connected.

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly n integers.

postconditions.expression: all(isinstance(x, int) and x >= 0 for x in output_values)
postconditions.description: Each output value is a non-negative integer.

postconditions.expression: all(output_values[i] == sum(sorted([min(distances[i][t] for t in towns_of_type[t]) for t in range(1, k + 1)])[0:s]) for i in range(n))
postconditions.description: For each town i, the output is the sum of the s smallest distances from town i to the nearest town producing each of the k goods types, where distances are shortest path lengths in the graph.
